question: Should OpenClaw adopt `openclaw commands list/inspect` as a distinct operator-facing catalog contract, or should the proposal converge on the existing Gateway `commands.list` inventory?
rationale: Both boundaries are technically plausible, but choosing the durable namespace, canonical data source, stable JSON fields, plugin metadata obligations, and Gateway relationship establishes product and compatibility policy that cannot be inferred from implementation quality alone.

options.title: Sponsor scoped Option A
options.body: Open the required discussion and accept a narrowly scoped operator CLI after explicitly defining its relationship to Gateway `commands.list` and its schema compatibility rules.

options.title: Converge on Gateway inventory
options.body: Revise the RFC so the CLI is a projection of one canonical Gateway-owned catalog rather than a separate joined contract.

options.title: Decline the new contract
options.body: Keep existing command-discovery surfaces and close the RFC and linked implementation work if the additional operator catalog is not worth its compatibility cost.

recommendation.title: Sponsor scoped Option A
recommendation.body: Open the required discussion and accept a narrowly scoped operator CLI after explicitly defining its relationship to Gateway `commands.list` and its schema compatibility rules.

likelyOwner.reason: They reviewed and merged the existing Gateway command catalog whose long-term relationship to this proposal is the central product decision.
